product_overview: A modular ERP backend platform providing security, organization master data, master data lookups, notifications, and file services. The system supports JWT-based authentication, role- and permission-driven access, hierarchical org structures, secure file token workflows, and channel-based notifications.
core_goals: Provide secure authentication, authorization, and user management
Support hierarchical organization master data and scoped data access
Enable admin management of pages, permissions, roles, and menus
Offer configurable master data lookup tables for cross-module reuse
Deliver secure file upload/download/delete flows using time-limited tokens
Support notification sending, templates, channel configuration, and inbox/history tracking

features.name: Authentication
features.description: Allows users to log in, refresh and revoke tokens, self-register, activate accounts, and request password resets.
user_flows: POST /api/auth/login with valid username and password -> Receive 200 with response.data.accessToken and response.data.expiresIn -> Use access token for protected API calls -> Receive 200 from authenticated endpoints
POST /api/auth/login with invalid credentials -> Receive 401 or 400 error response with success=false and error details
POST /api/auth/refresh with valid refresh-token HttpOnly cookie -> Receive 200 with response.data.accessToken and response.data.expiresIn -> Continue calling protected endpoints
POST /api/auth/logout with an active refresh token -> Receive 204 No Content -> POST /api/auth/refresh with the same cookie -> Receive 401 or 403 error

POST /api/auth/signup with valid username, email, and password -> Receive 200 with response.data.userId, response.data.username, and response.data.enabled=false -> POST /api/auth/signup/activate with a valid token -> Receive 200 OK

POST /api/auth/forgot-password with an unknown email -> Receive 200 OK generic response without revealing account existence -> POST /api/auth/reset-password with an invalid or expired token -> Receive error response
POST /api/auth/reset-password with a valid token and new password -> Receive 200 OK -> POST /api/auth/login with the new password -> Receive 200 with response.data.accessToken

POST /api/auth/login with a low-privilege user -> Receive 200 with response.data.accessToken -> GET /api/menu/user-menu with JWT bearer token -> Receive 200 with a reduced menu tree based on VIEW permissions

POST /api/auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with response.data.accessToken -> GET /api/menu/user-menu/{userId} as an authenticated admin -> Receive 200 with MenuItemDto[] for the specified user
GET /api/menu/user-menu without a JWT bearer token -> Receive 401 or 403 error response with success=false

tech_stack: Spring Security (JWT bearer auth via JwtAuthenticationFilter; FileTokenFilter for token-embedded file routes)

features.name: Authentication
features.description: Login, token refresh, logout, self-signup with activation, password reset. All endpoints public; login issues a short-lived JWT access token plus an HttpOnly refresh-token cookie. IMPORTANT - every JSON response in this API, including AuthController's, is auto-wrapped by a global @RestControllerAdvice (src/main/java/com/erp/common/web/advice/ApiResponseWrapper.java) into {success, message, data, error, timestamp, correlationId}. The actual payload (e.g. accessToken, expiresIn) is always nested under the top-level "data" key. Only raw byte[]/binary responses, Swagger/OpenAPI docs, and actuator endpoints are exempt.

endpoints.description: User login, returns short-lived JWT access token, wrapped in ApiResponse (read as response.data.accessToken)
Login returning full user info including roles/permissions, wrapped in ApiResponse (read as response.data.*)
Refresh access token using the refresh-token HttpOnly cookie, wrapped in ApiResponse (read as response.data.accessToken)
Self-registration; account disabled until activated, wrapped in ApiResponse (read as response.data.*)
Activate a self-registered account via emailed token
Request password reset email (always generic success, anti-enumeration)
Consume reset token, set new password

Remove a page (and all its perms) from role

features.name: File Management
features.description: File upload/download/delete via short-lived encrypted tokens (deliberately bypasses standard JWT auth for token-embedded routes), plus per-owner file listing via standard JWT.

endpoints.description: Issue a short-lived encrypted upload token
Issue download/delete access token, query param: action
Upload file (multipart) using the token issued above. Route is permitAll in SecurityConfig; actual auth enforced by FileTokenFilter validating the encrypted token, not JWT.
Download file using access token. Route is permitAll; gated by FileTokenFilter.

response_schema.200: raw byte[] with Content-Disposition attachment header

endpoints.description: Delete file using access token. Root-level single-segment DELETE is permitAll (Ant "/*"); gated by FileTokenFilter. Fragile design - any future single-segment DELETE mapping in another module would unintentionally become unauthenticated.

features.name: Notifications
features.description: Sending/scheduling notifications, per-user inbox (history/unread/mark-read), template management, and channel configuration.

endpoints.description: Schedule a future notification. KNOWN GAP: NOTIF_LOG has no column to persist scheduledAt, so the service dispatches immediately identical to /send, silently ignoring the requested time.
Get unread notifications summary. NON-FUNCTIONAL: annotated GOVERNANCE-NOTE-BLOCKED (DRV-NOTIF-003) -- NOTIF_LOG has no read/unread column, always throws HTTP 422 NOTIF_READ_TRACKING_UNAVAILABLE.
Mark notification as read. NON-FUNCTIONAL: same DRV-NOTIF-003 gap, always throws HTTP 422.
Search templates (filters templateCode, channelTypeId, moduleCode, isActiveFl)
Deactivate template (no reactivate endpoint exists, unlike Pages/Roles)
List channel configs (fixed small set, no pagination)

known_limitations.issue: Org Structure endpoints are the priority focus of this run - frontend was just rewired from mock/local-state to consume these real APIs
known_limitations.impact: Prioritize exercising create/update/search/activate/deactivate across all 7 entities (legal entities, branches, regions, departments, cost centers, profit centers, location sites) and the department/cost-center tree endpoints.

known_limitations.issue: GET /api/v1/notifications/unread and PUT /api/v1/notifications/{id}/read always fail with HTTP 422
known_limitations.impact: NOTIF_LOG has no read/unread column in the DB schema (see governance DRV-NOTIF-003); these endpoints exist only to satisfy API contract/frontend typing and cannot be exercised as functional in tests beyond asserting the 422 error.

known_limitations.issue: POST /api/v1/notifications/schedule ignores scheduledAt and dispatches immediately
known_limitations.impact: Consumers expecting deferred delivery will not get it; scheduledAt has no durable persistence column (DRV-NOTIF-004).

known_limitations.issue: ALL JSON responses (including AuthController's) are auto-wrapped by the global ApiResponseWrapper RestControllerAdvice into {success, message, data, error, timestamp, correlationId} -- the login accessToken is at response.data.accessToken, NOT top-level
known_limitations.impact: Any test code or client that reads response.accessToken directly instead of response.data.accessToken will fail immediately at login, cascading into every downstream authenticated test. This must be reflected in ALL generated test scripts.

known_limitations.issue: GET /api/menu/user-menu/{userId} has no visible admin-only gate at controller level
known_limitations.impact: Potential IDOR if service layer does not restrict this to admins -- any authenticated user might view another user's menu/permission structure. Worth an explicit auth test.

known_limitations.issue: GET /api/lookups/{lookupCode} requires full JWT auth despite being a generic dropdown-population endpoint for all modules
known_limitations.impact: Pre-login/public screens (e.g. signup form needing a COUNTRY dropdown) cannot call it without already being authenticated.

known_limitations.issue: PermissionController has no GET-by-ID and no DELETE endpoint
known_limitations.impact: Inconsistent with the CRUD pattern used elsewhere (RoleController, PageController); cannot fetch a single permission or remove one via the API.

known_limitations.issue: File token-embedded routes (/upload/**, /download/**, root-level single-segment DELETE) bypass the standard JWT filter entirely via permitAll
known_limitations.impact: Security rests solely on FileTokenFilter correctly validating the encrypted token; the DELETE /* matcher is scoped only by HTTP method + one path segment and could unintentionally expose any future root-level single-segment DELETE mapping as unauthenticated.

known_limitations.issue: No @PreAuthorize on any controller; fine-grained permission enforcement lives in the service layer
known_limitations.impact: Per-endpoint required permission codes (e.g. PERM_ROLE_CREATE) cannot be confirmed from controller source alone; only authenticated-vs-public can be verified from SecurityConfig, so permission-denial test cases need service-layer knowledge, not just controller inspection.

known_limitations.issue: Inconsistent CRUD completeness across similar modules
known_limitations.impact: Org-structure controllers (7 of them) have activate/deactivate but no DELETE at all (soft-delete-only by design); Notification Templates has no delete or reactivate. May be intentional but should not be assumed missing/broken by test generation.
